description: A product manager is deciding whether to implement a third-party auth service (fast to market) or build an in-house system (more control/security). They must analyze the long-term cost of technical debt vs. the immediate need for a product launch.

user_profile.context: Security audit is looming, need to decide on the architecture

fact_sheet.fact: The internal project to develop a new authentication system is codenamed 'Project Chimera'.
Ava Chen is the Product Manager responsible for the 'FinSecure Wallet' product launch.
The hard deadline for the 'FinSecure Wallet' product launch is October 15, 2024, to capture the Q4 market.
The third-party authentication service being evaluated is 'AuthZoid'.
AuthZoid's pricing is $0.025 per Monthly Active User (MAU) plus a flat fee of $1,200/month for the enterprise support plan.
The projected MAU for 'FinSecure Wallet' is 250,000 by the end of the first year of operation.
The estimated one-time cost to build the in-house authentication system is $185,000, covering engineering salaries and initial setup.
The estimated annual ongoing cost for maintaining the in-house system is $40,000 for infrastructure and licensing, plus 20% of a senior engineer's salary.
The in-house solution would require a team of 3 Senior Backend Engineers and 1 DevOps Engineer.
The engineering team estimates a 5-month timeline to build, test, and deploy the in-house authentication system.
AuthZoid's technical team confirmed that a standard integration can be completed in 3 weeks.
FinSecure must pass a SOC 2 Type II audit by December 1, 2024, to onboard its first enterprise client, 'Globex Corporation'.
AuthZoid is fully compliant with SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and GDPR.
Building the in-house system would require an external security audit by 'CyberGuard Analytics', costing an additional $25,000.
The sales contact at AuthZoid is Ben Carter, and his direct email is b.carter@authzoid.com.
AuthZoid's service level agreement (SLA) guarantees 99.95% uptime, but only with the enterprise support plan.
In a meeting on June 5, 2024, CTO Maria Rodriguez stated a preference for an in-house system to avoid vendor lock-in.
Lead Engineer Leo Valdez documented a concern that migrating away from AuthZoid's proprietary user IDs in the future would be a 6-month project.
The final decision on the build vs. buy strategy must be logged in JIRA ticket FSW-101 by July 1, 2024.
FinSecure's primary competitor, 'Koinlytics', launched their platform on May 20, 2024, and acquired 50,000 users in their first month.
A 'Finovate Insights' report from May 2024 shows a 15% quarter-over-quarter growth in the digital wallet market.
The proposed in-house solution would be built using Go and PostgreSQL, running on the company's existing Kubernetes cluster in Google Cloud Platform.
AuthZoid's data processing centers are located in AWS regions us-east-1 and eu-west-2, which meets FinSecure's data residency requirements.
FinSecure's Head of Legal, David Chen, confirmed on June 10, 2024, that AuthZoid's Data Processing Addendum (DPA) is acceptable.
The in-house solution would provide direct database access for internal analytics tools, a feature not available in AuthZoid's standard plan.
The CEO, Sarah Jenkins, emphasized in the last all-hands meeting that first-mover advantage in the current market is 'critical'.

user_needs.description: What are the product launch and security audit deadlines for the FinSecure Wallet?
What is AuthZoid's integration timeline versus the in-house build timeline for Project Chimera?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After establishing the project deadlines, the immediate next step is to compare how the timelines of the two options fit within those constraints.

user_needs.description: What is AuthZoid's pricing model and the projected first-year user count?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning that the third-party option is significantly faster, the next logical question for a data-driven PM is to evaluate its cost.

user_needs.description: What are the estimated one-time build cost and the annual maintenance cost components for the in-house system?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After assessing the cost of the 'buy' option, the user will immediately want to compare it against the cost of the 'build' option.

user_needs.description: What security compliances does AuthZoid already have?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: The looming SOC 2 audit deadline (established in N1) makes the compliance status of a third-party vendor a critical, high-priority concern that can be anticipated early.

user_needs.description: What is the additional cost for the in-house system's security audit?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: Once the user understands the compliance status of the vendor, they will want to know the specific compliance costs associated with the alternative in-house path.

user_needs.description: What concern was documented about future migration from AuthZoid?
What was the CTO's stated preference regarding vendor lock-in?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After learning about a specific technical risk (migration difficulty), the user would naturally want to know the opinion of the key technical stakeholder (CTO) on that very topic.

user_needs.description: How critical is speed to market for leadership, based on the CEO's recent guidance and recent competitor traction?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After seeing the timeline gap between vendor integration and an in-house build, a natural next question is how much leadership values speed to market in light of recent competitor momentum.

user_needs.description: What is the final decision deadline and where should it be logged?
